provenance.open_item: OI-206 (Task 2) / transfers docs/p3_granularity_ab_3_1b.md to the joint estimator
provenance.window_construction: span S measures centered on the query measure m_c: [m_c - S//2, m_c + (S-1-S//2)] clipped to the piece measure range; the window is every event in that measure range; sub_piece preserves absolute ticks. Nested by construction; 'whole' == all events.
provenance.dcml_alignment: WiR (When-in-Rome) GT; ticks aligned exactly as a8_rebaseline_measure via compare_analyses._dcml_time_spans over the whole-piece anchor regions, computed ONCE per piece and reused for every span (so the windowed-vs-whole accuracy DELTA is convention-robust). ROOT: compare_analyses.roots_agree; KEY-LOCAL: compare_rn._our_key_ident vs compare_rn._dcml_key_tonic(local_key).
provenance.cost_caveat: cost_curve is the PYTHON reference decoder's wall time (decode_piece, with the report-only 24-key posterior skipped as the study runs it, and the memos OFF); it gives the SHAPE of cost-vs-span, NOT the C++ producer latency. The absolute interactive latency is tools/notation_seams/noteseam_latency.json (OI-203); the two are never conflated (#19).
provenance.establishment: the whole-piece decode reproduces decode_parity_ref.json's committed 'selected' segments (i,j,tonic,is_major,class_key) + total_score per stem (a mismatch is a #13 STOP; the run refuses to publish). Windowed decodes reuse the identical decode_piece on sub_pieces.
provenance.content_memo: correctness-preserving speedups: (1) score_segment_content memoized by (stem, abs_start, abs_end, tonic, is_major, class-tuple, frozenset(seg_pcs)) so overlapping windows of one piece re-use identical content scores; (2) the DP transition factors chord_trans_logp/key_trans_logp/entry_logp memoized (pure, piece-independent). BOTH ESTABLISHED (#19) memo-ON == memo-OFF byte-identical on sample windows; the cost_curve times with the memos OFF (the production decoder has no such memo).
provenance.cost_curve_sample: 109 of 109 pieces (evenly strided; cost is the SHAPE)
provenance.coverage: DECLARED corpus-representative sample: every 3th name-sorted piece = 109 of 326 covered pieces (the corpus is a homogeneous Bach-chorale set, so a name stride spans the size range evenly). Every downbeat in each sampled piece is queried. Chosen for tractability of the pure-Python reference decode (~20-30 s/piece x 326 ~ 2-3 h full); the FULL-corpus run is a mechanical extension of this same instrument with no --stride (no code change).

stability_rises_monotonically_with_span.claim: the fraction of queries whose reading equals the whole-piece reading rises monotonically with span size and reaches ~1.0 at 'whole' by construction

most_queries_stable_below_whole.claim: on this chorale-scale corpus MOST queries stabilize at a BOUNDED window well below the whole piece (a local reading needs only local context)
most_queries_stable_below_whole.band: fraction of queries whose smallest-stable span is a bounded (< whole) window >= 0.60; median smallest-stable width <= 16 measures

stability_fraction_at_small_spans.claim: count stability vs whole-piece is already high at 8 measures and higher at 16

accuracy_cost_of_bounding_is_small_but_n.claim: unlike the 3.1b legacy finding (window BEAT whole on Mozart), on the CHORALE-scale established envelope WHOLE-piece is the measured-accurate form, so bounding the span COSTS a little root/key-local accuracy; the cost shrinks as the span grows
accuracy_cost_of_bounding_is_small_but_n.band: root_agree@whole - root_agree@16 in [-0.01, +0.05] (whole >= windowed within ~5pp); key_local@whole - key_local@16 in [-0.01, +0.06]; both deltas larger at span 8

accuracy_sensitive_class.claim: the worst accuracy drops at small spans are pieces with long modulation spans / pieces whose global context revises the opening key (the desk-sim S2 retroactive-revision shape) — key-local drops more than root
accuracy_sensitive_class.band: the worst-drop pieces show a key-local drop at span 8 materially larger than the corpus mean; key-local is the more span-sensitive axis than root

cost_grows_with_span.claim: Python-reference decode wall time grows with span (roughly linear-to-superlinear in measures), so a bounded window is far cheaper to decode COLD than the whole piece
cost_grows_with_span.band: mean decode seconds monotone non-decreasing in span; mean@8 < mean@whole
